packageRules.description: LLM SDKs — high-touch. One PR per package, NEVER automerge, smoke-test required before human merge. INV-3 means an LLM-SDK bump can silently shift triage outputs; treat every release as load-bearing.

Front-end binaries (Joern, CodeQL CLI, OpenTofu, semgrep). These are vendored via the GitHub-Actions workflow YAML, not pyproject.toml — see the customManagers block below for how they're tracked. A wrong bump here can shift CPG fidelity (INV-6) or detector recall (INV-4) silently, so NEVER automerge.
Pre-1.0 deps (ruff, mypy at <1.0 historically) — manual review, no automerge. Pre-1.0 packages have no semver contract; patch releases can ship breaking changes.

Post-1.0 patch + minor — grouped into one weekly PR, automerged if CI passes. The npm + pypi communities treat post-1.0 semver as binding; if a package breaks that contract, move it to per-package review.
Major bumps anywhere — always manual. Read the migration guide; the PR body should link to it.
Dev dependencies (linters, types, test infra) — more permissive. Grouped + automerged.
GitHub Actions — pinned by SHA preferred; renovate keeps the SHA + comment in sync. Group all action bumps into one weekly PR.
Docker base images — patch + minor automerge after the 3-day soak. Major Postgres or Python image bumps are manual (could be a runtime regression).

customManagers.description: Track pinned tool versions in .github/workflows/*.yml that aren't in pyproject.toml or package.json (e.g. cosign, syft, trivy installed via direct binary download). Convention: comment line `# renovate: datasource=<x> depName=<y>` immediately before the `TOOL_VERSION: "X.Y.Z"` line.
Track Docker base-image SHA pins in Dockerfiles when written as `FROM image:tag@sha256:<digest>`. Renovate maintains both the tag and digest in lockstep.
